hook: I need information from a government office.
hook_q: How do I file an RTI?

slides.title: Every citizen has this right.
slides.body: Under the RTI Act, all citizens have the right to information, subject to the Act's provisions.

slides.title: Write your request.
slides.body: Apply to the Public Information Officer in writing or electronically, in English, Hindi or the area's official language. You don't have to give a reason.

slides.title: Pay ₹10 for central government offices.
slides.body: Pay by cash, demand draft, banker's cheque, postal order, or online where available. States set their own fees. Below the poverty line? No fee, with your BPL certificate.

slides.title: Central offices: apply online.
slides.body: For many Government of India offices, you can file the application and pay the fee online at rtionline.gov.in.

slides.title: Reply within 30 days.
slides.body: The officer must reply within 30 days. If the information concerns someone's life or liberty, within 48 hours.

slides.title: Late reply? It's free.
slides.body: If the office misses the time limit, the information must be given to you free of charge.

slides.title: Not satisfied? Appeal.
list: First appeal: within 30 days, to an officer senior to the PIO
Second appeal: within 90 days, to the Central or State Information Commission

caption:
Need information from a government office? Use your Right to Information. 👇

1️⃣ Every citizen has the right to information under the RTI Act
2️⃣ Apply in writing or online, in English, Hindi or the local official language. No reason needed
3️⃣ Fee: ₹10 for central government offices (states set their own). No fee for BPL applicants (with a BPL certificate)
4️⃣ Reply due in 30 days, or 48 hours if life or liberty is involved
5️⃣ Late reply? The information is free
6️⃣ First appeal within 30 days, second appeal to the Information Commission within 90 days

Source: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Sec 3, 6, 7, 19); RTI Rules, 2012
